claims.statement: DatabaseManager resolves the SQLite database at `app_data_dir/meeting_minutes.sqlite`; if that file is absent it copies the legacy `meeting_minutes.db` from the same directory over it when present or creates a new database, then connects and runs the embedded `sqlx::migrate!("./migrations")` set on every open.

If opening the database fails with an error message containing `malformed` or `corrupt`, DatabaseManager deletes the orphaned `meeting_minutes.sqlite-wal` and `-shm` files and retries the open exactly once; any other error, or a second failure, propagates.

On application exit, `RunEvent::Exit` calls `DatabaseManager::cleanup()`, which runs `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` to flush WAL pages into the main database file and then closes the connection pool; a checkpoint failure is logged but non-fatal.

First launch is detected solely by the absence of `meeting_minutes.sqlite`; startup then skips manager construction and emits a delayed `first-launch-detected` event, and `AppState` is created afterwards by the onboarding commands `import_and_initialize_database` or `initialize_fresh_database`, the latter seeding default `builtin-ai` summary and `parakeet` transcription config rows before both emit `database-initialized`.

Legacy database import accepts either a `.db` file, a directory containing `meeting_minutes.db`, or a repository root containing `backend/meeting_minutes.db`; `DatabaseManager::import_legacy_database` copies the selected file to `app_data_dir/meeting_minutes.db` and re-runs the standard open sequence so the copy-from-legacy branch migrates it into the `.sqlite` database.

The initial schema creates `meetings`, `transcripts`, `summary_processes`, `transcript_chunks`, `settings`, and `transcript_settings`; content tables reference `meetings(id)` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`, and `summary_processes` and `transcript_chunks` use `meeting_id` as their primary key, so both hold at most one row per meeting.

Migration `20251006000000` adds `meetings.folder_path` — the link between a meeting row and its on-disk recording folder — and the `transcripts.audio_start_time`, `audio_end_time`, and `duration` columns (REAL seconds from recording start) used for audio-transcript playback synchronization.

Additive migrations extend `settings` with per-provider configuration columns — `openRouterApiKey` (added by a temporary-table rebuild), `ollamaEndpoint`, the `customOpenAIConfig` JSON blob, and `geminiApiKey`.

Several schema surfaces are not exercised by compiled code: `transcripts.speaker` and the legacy `summary`/`action_items`/`key_points` columns are never written by the transcript INSERT paths and `speaker` is absent from the `Transcript` model; `settings.geminiApiKey` is missing from the `Setting` model and the provider-to-column maps; and the `licensing` and `meeting_notes` tables created by migrations have no referencing module in the frontend crate.

`TranscriptsRepository::save_transcript` creates the meeting (id `meeting-{uuid}`) and all of its transcript segments (`transcript-{uuid}` ids) in a single transaction and persists the optional `folder_path`; paginated transcript reads order segments by `audio_start_time ASC` for playback sync.

`MeetingsRepository::update_meeting_name` updates both `meetings.title` and the denormalized `transcript_chunks.meeting_name` in one transaction (used after summary generation extracts a title), and `delete_meeting` removes `transcript_chunks`, `summary_processes`, `transcripts`, then the meeting itself inside an explicit transaction.

`summary_processes` implements regeneration safety: `create_or_reset_process` upserts a `PENDING` row and, on conflict, copies the existing `result` into `result_backup` with a timestamp; `update_process_completed` overwrites `result` and clears the backup, while `update_process_failed` and `update_process_cancelled` restore it via `result = COALESCE(result_backup, result)`.

`settings` and `transcript_settings` are managed as singleton rows (`id='1'`) through upserts; provider names map to concrete API-key columns (`openai`→`openaiApiKey`, `claude`→`anthropicApiKey`, `openrouter`→`openRouterApiKey`, etc.), `builtin-ai` and `parakeet` are keyless no-ops, and `custom-openai` is deliberately rejected by `save_api_key`/`get_api_key` in favor of the `customOpenAIConfig` JSON blob.

`api_process_transcript` stores the full transcript text plus the model, model name, and chunking parameters in the single `transcript_chunks` row via upsert, defaulting `chunk_size` to 40000 and `overlap` to 1000 when not provided — a provenance record, not a segmentation of the text.

`create_meeting_folder` builds `{base}/{Sanitized_Name}_{YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM}/` with an optional `.checkpoints/` subdirectory, where the base comes from `get_default_recordings_folder()`: `%USERPROFILE%\Music\meetily-recordings` on Windows, `~/Movies/meetily-recordings` on macOS, `~/Documents/meetily-recordings` on other platforms, each with a Documents (then `.`) fallback.

`RecordingSaver::start_accumulation(auto_save)` always creates the meeting folder, `transcripts.json`, and `metadata.json`, but creates `.checkpoints/` and the `IncrementalAudioSaver` only when `auto_save` is true; when disabled, audio chunks are consumed and discarded (transcription already happened upstream) and `metadata.audio_file` is an empty string.

`IncrementalAudioSaver` encodes a `.checkpoints/audio_chunk_{NNN}.mp4` checkpoint whenever its buffer reaches 30 seconds of samples (`sample_rate * 30`); `finalize()` flushes the remainder, merges all checkpoints into `audio.mp4` with the FFmpeg concat demuxer (`-f concat -safe 0 -c copy`, no re-encoding), and deletes `.checkpoints/` (non-fatally); the `recover_audio_from_checkpoints`, `cleanup_checkpoints`, and `has_audio_checkpoints` commands expose the same directory for crash recovery.

`transcripts.json` is a `version: "1.0"` document whose segments carry `audio_start_time`/`audio_end_time`/`duration` in seconds from recording start — the playback-sync contract shared with the `transcripts` table; it is written atomically (temp file, verification, rename), the live saver upserts segments by `sequence_id` and rewrites the file on every segment, and import/retranscription share the same format through `audio/common.rs::write_transcripts_json`.

`metadata.json` is written atomically and starts at `status: "recording"`; `stop_and_save` transitions it to `status: "completed"` with `completed_at` and `duration_seconds` (the recording-state duration, falling back to the last segment's `audio_end_time`); import writes a `source: "import"` variant with the real meeting id, and retranscription read-modify-writes it to add `retranscribed_at` and drop `detected_summary_language`.

`metadata.json` also carries per-meeting summary language fields — `summary_language` (user override) and `detected_summary_language` (cached auto-detection) — maintained under a global write lock with a read-modify-write that preserves all other fields and normalizes codes (`zh-tw` preserved, `zh-cn` → `zh`, other regional subtags stripped); meetings without a `folder_path` report `storage: "local_fallback"` instead of metadata storage.

Stopping a live recording deliberately does not write SQLite: the Rust side finalizes the folder files and emits `recording-stopped` carrying `folder_path` and `meeting_name`, after which the frontend calls `api_save_transcript`, which transactionally inserts the `meetings` row (with `folder_path`) and all `transcripts` rows.

Retranscription locates the audio file inside the existing meeting folder (`audio.mp4` first, then other known names, then any audio extension), deletes and re-inserts the meeting's `transcripts` rows within one transaction, and rewrites `transcripts.json` and `metadata.json`.

Audio import creates a checkpoint-less meeting folder under the recordings base, copies the source to `audio.{ext}`, writes the meeting and transcript rows in one transaction via `create_meeting_with_transcripts`, then writes `transcripts.json` and `metadata.json`; cancellation removes the folder.

Three Tauri store JSON files are owned by specific modules via `tauri_plugin_store::StoreExt` (file placement owned by the plugin): `onboarding-status.json` (key `status`, `OnboardingStatus` including parakeet/summary model-download state) by `onboarding.rs`; `recording_preferences.json` (key `preferences`) by `audio::recording_preferences`; and `store.json` (key `authToken`) only read by a dead-code helper in `api.rs`, since live commands receive the auth token as an argument.

`complete_onboarding` persists the `builtin-ai` summary config and `parakeet` transcription config to SQLite before marking onboarding complete in the store, so a crash cannot leave a completed flag without its model configuration.

Notification settings are not a Tauri store: `ConsentManager` serializes `NotificationSettings` (consent, system permission, manual DND, per-type preferences with `meeting_reminder_minutes` defaulting to `[15, 5]`) directly to `<config_dir>/meetily/notifications.json`, creating the parent directory on demand.

Model binaries live under the app data directory, resolved at startup via Tauri path APIs: `app_data_dir/models` for Whisper and Parakeet (created by their `set_models_directory` initializers) and `app_data_dir/models/summary` for built-in AI GGUF models.
